Chapter 3. Creating a Secret Refuge: The Hidden Annex and Daily Life in Hiding.
Turning an ordinary office into a true sanctuary took more than just clever planning. It meant living every day with your senses on high alert—always watching, always listening, never letting your guard down. Imagine this: the back rooms of a quiet building, tucked away behind a movable bookcase. That’s where the hidden annex was created, where the family hoped they could ride out the storm together.
Setting up the space wasn’t just about moving a few chairs. Every move had to be made in secret. Supplies were gathered quietly, furniture rearranged late at night, all to avoid drawing any attention. The woman and her husband worked long after dark, sometimes with a couple of trusted friends by their side. Each action felt like a small, brave push back against the fear closing in around them.
Once they settled in, life changed in ways they couldn’t have imagined. The annex was tight, with barely enough space for everyone and almost no privacy. Going outside was out of the question. Every sound had to be hushed, and even simple things like walking or opening a cupboard were timed to avoid making noise for the workers below. Days stretched on, slow and repetitive, only broken up by the arrival of food, a scrap of news, or the rare treat their helpers risked to bring in.
The woman became their lifeline to the world beyond those walls. She brought groceries, books, and little updates, each one more precious than gold. She learned her way around the city’s black market, bartering for ration cards and searching for anything that might bring a moment of comfort. Every trip outside was a risk—one misstep could mean disaster for everyone. But she kept going, driven by duty and the hope that even the smallest kindness could make a difference.
Inside, the stress sometimes bubbled over. Being packed together, day after day, meant nerves got frayed. Small arguments broke out, and there were times when hope felt almost impossible to hold onto. Yet, even in the toughest moments, there were small joys—shared meals, a quiet laugh, the comfort of not being alone. The younger daughter, always restless and full of dreams, filled notebook after notebook with her thoughts, while the others clung to routine and each other’s company.
The woman’s visits were more than just supply runs—they were a lifeline. She’d listen, offer encouragement, and do her best to keep her own worries to herself. It became clear that survival wasn’t just about staying hidden. It was about holding onto your humanity, even when fear threatened to take over.
The annex was so much more than a secret hiding place. It was a powerful reminder of what ordinary people can do to protect each other, even in the darkest circumstances. Every single day, they proved that resistance can come in many forms—and sometimes, it’s the small acts of care that matter most, keeping hope alive when everything else feels impossible.
